set.approach: This is the first line you see when driving into the gorges. There are two usual ways in: either by parking at the Acropole des Draveurs and walking over the frozen river, or by starting at the Draveur visitor centre, passing over the dam and then returning along the far bank toward the cliff. Coming from the south, the Pin Blanc campground is another start, and that way also crosses the river on ice.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. The third pitch ends on a big snow ramp with bolts, which is the place to note for the way down. From the trees at the top, work back down to the bolts below the last pitch, then keep descending down climber's left. The final rappel can be skipped by walking off to climber's left along a narrow goat-style path that bypasses the first pitch on the right. The lower pitches are somewhat sheltered from overhead hazard by the snow ramp.

review.notes: Route page: location, crossing options, bolted descent line and climber's-left walk-off. Area page: the river crossings.

set.approach: From the river-side path, head straight toward the big stalactites, climbing through forest and scree. To reach the river path, use the Draveur visitor centre on the north side, which crosses the river by the dam, or the southern approach from the Pin Blanc campground, which crosses on the ice.

review.notes: Route page: head for the stalactites from the river path. Area page: the two ways to reach the river path. No descent stated on the page.

set.approach: This is the widest, most obvious ice flow north of Le Triolet. From the Draveur visitor centre, cross the river at the dam and follow the path along the west bank to the base.

review.notes: Route page: obvious flow north of Le Triolet, approach from the visitor centre along the west-side path. Area page: northern approach crosses by the dam.

set.approach: The route sits above C'est pas la mer à Ciboire. After topping out that line, cross a snowy slab to reach the base, where a fixed anchor with rappel rings marks the start.

review.notes: Route page: located above the WI5 line; snow slab to a fixed anchor. Area page: access. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Draveur visitor centre, follow the river trail (trail 7) for a short distance until a big yellow ice formation shows up on your left higher in the valley. No marked trail leads to the base, so expect to make your own way up.

review.notes: Route page: trail 7 from the visitor centre, yellow formation, no official trail. Area page: access as for the park.

set.approach: In winter the park road is travelled on skis, usually towing a sled, to reach the Équerre sector. The first part of the walk to the base shares the trail to La Pomme d'or; then bear left up a steep snow slope. The final pillar is in view for much of the approach.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route on Abalakov threads, rock horns and old fixed slings, and replace anything doubtful. The second pitch is a snow slope where a rappel is awkward: walk backward down it with the rope kept tight, and clip a small tree about five metres above the last anchor as a redirect, since a swing on this traverse could be serious.

review.notes: Route page: shared approach with La Pomme d'or then left, rappel the route, snow-slope rappel technique. Park pages: winter ski/sled access.

set.approach: In winter the park road is travelled on skis, usually towing a sled, to reach the Équerre sector. The first part of the walk shares the trail to La Pomme d'or; then continue left up a steep snow slope. The final pillar is visible for most of the approach. This variation starts on the Cascade 74 line and joins La Loutre higher up.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route on Abalakov threads, rock horns and old fixed slings, and replace anything doubtful. The second pitch is a snow slope where a rappel is awkward: walk backward down it with the rope kept tight, and clip a small tree about five metres above the last anchor as a redirect, since a swing on this traverse could be serious.

review.notes: Route page: same approach and descent wording for this variation; starts on Cascade 74.

set.approach: This short mixed variation is reached by first climbing four pitches of La Pomme d'or. The start is on a broad ledge a few metres to the left of the fixed anchor there, and the line works up a crack that leans out and angles right to the ice curtain above.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): start is five metres left of the fixed anchor after four pitches of La Pomme d'or. No descent stated.

set.approach: In winter the park road is travelled on skis, usually towing a sled, to reach the Équerre sector. From the river below the climb, scout the line up the talus and snowfield. Other starts exist, but the main line takes a narrow corner high in a couloir, out of sight from below.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. A line of V-threads often marks the way down later in the season, but inspect any thread before trusting it.

review.notes: Route page: scouting up talus and snowfield, hidden corner start, camping, V-thread line for the way down.

set.approach: In winter the park road is travelled on skis, usually towing a sled, to reach the Équerre sector. The start is the same as La Pomme d'or: begin up its first pitch, then continue straight up instead of traversing left.
set.descent_text: The best way down is to rappel La Pomme d'or, whose top anchor lies well to the left of this route's top-out. That anchor can be hard to find among dense vegetation and the complex edge of the cliff. Rappelling the route itself is difficult because the line traverses.

review.notes: Route page: Location says same start as La Pomme d'or then straight; its own Description states the descent.

set.approach: Walk the trail on the east side of the river to about kilometre 5 of the park road, where the wide waterfall comes into view. Follow the stream up to its base.

review.notes: Route page (French): see the fall near km 5, follow the stream up. Area page: trail 6 or 7.

set.approach: Use the east-side trail along the river. The route is the left-hand fall of the pair of cascades that lie between Bilbo and Gandalf. The second pitch is simply a walk up the river bed to the main waterfall.

review.notes: Route page (French/English): left of the duo; second pitch is walking up the river. Area page: trail 6 or 7.

set.approach: Walk past the Équerre sector campground, then take the Chute-du-ruisseau-blanc trail a short way to reach the waterfall.

review.notes: Route page: campground, ruisseau blanc trail, rappel on trees. Area page: all routes lie east of the river.

set.approach: Stay on the main east-bank trail, well beyond the Équerre shelter. In clear weather the top pitch can be spotted from the trail. Then leave the trail and bushwhack up the creek, which usually carries deep snow.
set.descent_text: Rappel from trees and Abalakov threads.

review.notes: Route page (French typos): main east-side trail, third pitch visible, bushwhack up creek, rappel on trees and Abalakovs.

set.approach: All routes in this sector are on the east side of the river. The line is a finish for Passion Tropicale: it shares that route's opening pitch and then takes a thinner, steeper exit to the right.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): shares first pitch with Passion Tropicale, right-hand exit. Area page: east of river. No descent stated.

set.approach: The route lies directly behind the Équerre shelter, on the east side of the river. Use the shelter as the landmark for finding it.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, using a pair of ropes.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): behind the shelter; map and guide misplace it; rappel with two ropes. Area page: east side.

set.approach: Parking is limited to a couple of cars at the start of the access road, with an overflow lot near the bridge. The approach crosses private land, so keep to the signed route and go on foot or snowshoes only, since skis are not allowed. Walk the access road without a vehicle, then take the signed trail on the right at the first marker. Keep left at the forks, following the federation's arrows, and at the third marker follow the blue-flagged track up through large boulders to the foot of the climbs. Aurorae is on the left-hand sector, a steep caramel-coloured flow.

review.notes: Area page and topo: access route; both describe the same private-land trail. Route page: left section. No descent stated.

set.approach: Parking is limited to a couple of cars at the start of the access road, with an overflow lot near the bridge. The approach crosses private land, so keep to the signed route and go on foot or snowshoes only, since skis are not allowed. Walk the access road without a vehicle, then take the signed trail on the right at the first marker. Keep left at the forks, following the federation's arrows, and at the third marker follow the blue-flagged track up through large boulders to the foot of the climbs. L'Imbu is just right of Aurorae, on the far right of the left-hand sector.

review.notes: As for Aurorae. Route page: far right of the left section. No descent stated.

set.approach: Parking is limited to a couple of cars at the start of the access road, with an overflow lot near the bridge. The approach crosses private land, so keep to the signed route and go on foot or snowshoes only, since skis are not allowed. Walk the access road without a vehicle, then take the signed trail on the right at the first marker. Keep left at the forks, following the federation's arrows, and at the third marker follow the blue-flagged track up through large boulders to the foot of the climbs. From the left end of the crag, this is the first route that is blue rather than yellow or orange.

review.notes: As for Aurorae. Route page: first blue route from the left. Topo lists it as Masturbabination with a slightly harder grade than the row's. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start at the Dôme lot beside Route 381 and follow the hiking trail beyond two cabins until the waterfall shows, then strike off through the woods to the route. The line sits toward the right-hand end of the mountain's south-facing cliff.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): location and tree rappel. Area page: trail past two cabins, then into the woods toward the ice flow.

set.approach: All the winter lines here begin at the extreme right end of the main wall, to the right of the rock route L'entonnoir. This route starts there and is more an alpine walk than a climb. A fall would be serious because the base of the wall is high and vertical.
set.descent_text: Walk off over the top to rejoin the trail, which lies a short distance straight up from the exit.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): can walk back on top to the trail. Area page: all routes start at the right end of the main wall.

set.approach: All the winter lines here begin at the extreme right end of the main wall, to the right of the rock route L'entonnoir. Climb to a small corner facing right, set on a wooded ledge; a short ladder and a bolt with a cable there can be covered by ice. The opening matches La Randonnée, after which the line goes straight up.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): same start as La Randonnée; corner with ladder and cable. Area page: right end of main wall. No descent stated.

set.approach: All the winter lines here begin at the extreme right end of the main wall, to the right of the rock route L'entonnoir. Climb to a small corner facing right, set on a wooded ledge; a short ladder and a bolt with a cable there may be iced over. From there climb directly up the corner and pass the bolt.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): same corner, straight up past the bolt. Area page: right end of main wall. No descent stated.

set.approach: All the winter lines here begin at the extreme right end of the main wall, to the right of the rock route L'entonnoir. The route follows a short wall to a good ledge, then a series of small ledges and slabs.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual) and area page: right end of the main wall. Start details are thin. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the parking lot at the reception chalet of the Grands-Jardins park, take the trail toward Lac Pioui and turn off at the signed junction for Mont de l'Ours early on the trail. At the base of the mountain, continue left to a leaning dihedral, which is where the line starts.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): continue left to a lying dihedral. Area page: trail to the junction. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the parking lot at the reception chalet of the Grands-Jardins park, take the trail toward Lac Pioui and turn off at the signed junction for Mont de l'Ours early on the trail. The Ricard flow is the only ice line visible from the road and is easy to recognise. The route starts up that flow, then continues up the gully above it.

review.notes: Route page: Ricard flow visible from road; belays on trees then glue-ins. Federation supplement states the descent is by rappel in the route. Area page: trail.

set.approach: From the parking lot at the reception chalet of the Grands-Jardins park, take the trail toward Lac Pioui and turn off at the signed junction for Mont de l'Ours early on the trail. The route is on the north face of the mountain. Start in an open, right-leaning dihedral; two bolts are visible some way up.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the rings at the top anchor. The pitch is only just within reach of a single long rope, so check the length before you commit.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): north face, open dihedral with bolts visible; rap rings at top.

set.approach: From the parking lot at the reception chalet of the Grands-Jardins park, take the trail toward Lac Pioui and turn off at the signed junction for Mont de l'Ours early on the trail. The line lies left of La coulée Ricard and right of the rock climbs of the Directe sector, on the south face, and it follows small ice sections up the wall.

review.notes: Route page and federation supplement agree on the position between the Directe and the Ricard flow. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the parking lot at the reception chalet of the Grands-Jardins park, take the trail toward Lac Pioui and turn off at the signed junction for Mont de l'Ours early on the trail. The Ricard flow is the only ice line visible from the road and is easy to recognise; the climb is high on the mountain from the very start.
set.descent_text: Belay and rappel from a tree at the top of the gully.

review.notes: Route page (bilingual): anchor and rappel on a tree; approach via the park trail.
